result.title: Can AI Design a Better nnU-Net? A Hypothesis-Driven Architecture Discovery Loop from Failures to Design Rules
result.summary: Neural architecture search and LLM-driven evolution often reduce evaluation to a scalar fitness score, discarding failures that could explain why designs succeed or fail. We present a hypothesis-driven architecture discovery loop in which LLM agents diagnose structured error patterns, formulate falsifiable hypotheses, test counterfactual controls under a frozen nnU-Net pipeline, and distill validated mechanisms into executable trigger-to-action rules. Across eight search waves, the loop identifies two principles for 3D medical image segmentation. First, reallocating computation from high-resolution decoders to the mid-encoder preserves thin-anatomy boundaries while reducing cost. Second, support-confined region contrast addresses errors between nested anatomical compartments, with anatomy-dependent triggers selecting when the rule applies. These principles produce LeanNeXt (0.78 MACs and 0.92 training-step time relative to nnU-Net; +1.63 Dice points on four-fold KiTS23 cross-validation) and trigger-routed LeanNeXt+. The latter improves all 15 evaluated CT/MRI settings over nnU-Net and exceeds the 3.3 larger ResEnc-M on 12 of 15 benchmarks at 0.30 its parameter count. Relative to random sampling, one-shot LLM generation, and score-selected agent search, the loop shows how failure analysis can yield reusable design rules across modalities.

AI.brief_summary: 提出由 LLM agent 驱动的假设式架构发现循环：分析结构化误差、提出可证伪假设、在冻结的 nnU-Net 上做反事实对照，再把验证过的机制蒸馏成可执行的 trigger-to-action 规则，用于 3D 医学分割并得到 LeanNeXt/LeanNeXt+。
AI.relevance_reason: 其以失败误差驱动假设、用反事实对照分配贡献并沉淀为条件触发规则的做法，可能为 VLM 推理的轨迹监督、贡献分配以及「何时触发某步计算」的决策提供可核查线索，但研究对象是分割架构而非多模态推理状态，需核查可迁移性。
